claims.text: The initial alloy is as-cast equiatomic HfMoTaTiZr.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high mechanical performance at room and elevated temperatures.
The proposed intervention is to replace all or most of the Hf atomic fraction with Zr.
Replacing Hf with Zr will reduce the alloy density.
The Hf-to-Zr substitution will retain a BCC solid-solution structure.
Hf and Zr have sufficiently similar atomic radii and chemical compatibility to preserve lattice distortion after substitution.
Preserving lattice distortion and the BCC solid solution will largely retain solid-solution strengthening.
Zr has a significantly lower atomic weight and density than Hf.
Zr is chemically and crystallographically compatible with the other refractory elements in the proposed alloy.
Retaining Mo and Ta should help preserve elevated-temperature strength because these high-melting elements promote elevated-temperature strength.
The modified alloy will retain high-temperature stability after full or near-full Hf replacement.
The modified alloy is expected to have a density of approximately 8–9 g/cm³.
The modified alloy is expected to retain yield strength and ductility comparable to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr at room temperature.
The modified alloy is expected to retain mechanical performance comparable to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr at temperatures around 1000 °C.
The stated applicability boundary is room temperature through approximately 1000 °C under standard compressive or tensile loading rates.
Full or partial Hf substitution may cause uncertain changes in strengthening or phase distribution.
The proposed experiment compares density, XRD phase constitution, yield or fracture strength, and ductility of substituted and baseline alloys at room temperature and approximately 1000 °C.
The hypothesis is rejected if density decreases but yield strength or ductility falls below 90% of the baseline value at either room temperature or approximately 1000 °C.
